limits: Requires matching M10-DEVICES-VM-v1 exact-artifact hardware and removable-media acceptance
Only original 7-Zip 26.06 x64 MSI and console executable/DLL; Windows GUI and shell integration are unavailable
One protected Windows job and one Windows thread on one assigned processor; ZIP examples use -mmt=off
Windows heap 32 MiB, owned page budget 10000 pages, demand-grown stack up to 8 MiB; one writer up to 8 MiB
Native extent volume: 1024 entries, 63-byte components, 64-MiB native file limit; Windows I/O has separate bounds
Selected Win64 APIs and a digest-pinned MSI console adapter, not a general Windows Installer service
Named x86-64 VMware/QEMU BIOS and UEFI profiles only; Secure Boot disabled; no physical/ARM qualification
Fresh installation and same-build recovery; cross-release application migration is unqualified
Single local account without authentication or native ACLs; Windows writes are brokered to current user data
Real native scalable framebuffer UI; no Windows GPU acceleration, DirectX or universal device support
Native app capabilities and dependencies retain their documented M7.4 limits; no human usability study
Bounded buffered software 2D composition and optional automatic VMware SVGA II presentation; no 3D or universal GPU driver
Installation requires a supported native controller with read/write/flush, 512-byte logical sectors and a 2-GiB to 2-TiB target; no 4Kn installation
Partially off-screen windows retain a reachable title-bar grip; no multi-monitor desktop
Hardware inventory: 128 PCI functions; eight USB devices on one supported xHCI controller; unsupported functions stay explicit
US QWERTY/Dvorak and descriptor-proven mouse wheel; unfamiliar report layouts retain boot input
Removable writes: clean mirrored FAT32, BOT, 512-byte sectors and verified flush; UAS write support unavailable
First supported FAT32 volume; create-only file copies up to 64 MiB; ASCII export names 63 bytes, graphical import names 55 bytes
Bounded contiguous free-space/directory search; no directory growth, exFAT/NTFS write, overwrite or repair
Copy is synchronous with keep-connected feedback; failures can require offline FAT checking; no power-loss atomicity guarantee
USB file transfer does not qualify USB OS installation or partition formatting; those operations are refused
Ethernet/Wi-Fi expansion, audio expansion, vendor GPU 3D, Steam gaming and physical/ARM profiles remain later phases
64-MiB OVMF: USB storage connects after installed startup; boot-attached USB storage/init allocation remains a recorded unqualified failure. Standard VMware package uses 128 MiB.
